solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Once VAT is settled there's little money

indicators.note: letters that are settled have been sorted out and put into a new, final order

blocks.note: the two words taken as written

explanation.surface: Once the tax bill has been paid, there is not much cash left over.
explanation.definitionFit: A centavo is a small coin worth one hundredth of a peso or real in Latin American currencies.

clue.text: Muslim leader in American state briefly

indicators.note: briefly means in shortened form, so the name is cut to its standard short form

blocks.note: a US state, cut to its short postal-style form of five letters

explanation.surface: A Muslim leader living in a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Calif is a variant spelling of caliph, the title of a ruler of the Islamic community.

clue.text: In which mostly Tory dailies bluster

definitions.text: In which mostly Tory dailies bluster

indicators.note: mostly means not all of it, so the last letter of the next word goes
to bluster is to blow about wildly, so the letters are tossed into disorder

blocks.note: Tory without its last letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A jibe at right-wing newspapers that rant.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: leader columns are where conservative papers sound off.
explanation.definitionFit: Editorials are a newspaper's opinion columns, the place where a paper states, or blusters, its views.

clue.text: Shirt present right away causing a laugh

indicators.note: right away means the letter for right is sent off from the word before

blocks.note: a tee is a T-shirt
here means in attendance, present
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A shirt given as a gift raises a giggle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' looks like a gift; it means in attendance.
explanation.definitionFit: A tee-hee is a suppressed or nervous giggle, a kind of laugh.

clue.text: Trees with bark cut off in one section

indicators.note: cut off means the end is lopped, so the last letter goes
in places the shortened word inside the two pieces that follow

blocks.note: a means one
tapa is the bark of the paper mulberry, beaten into cloth
s. is the abbreviation for section

explanation.surface: Trees whose bark has been stripped in one part of a wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bark' looks like the outer layer of the trees; it is a particular bark cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Atap, or attap, is the nipa palm, whose leaves are used for thatching in Malaysia.

clue.text: French poetry associated with outstanding fashion designer

blocks.note: vers is French for verse
ace means excellent

explanation.surface: French verse linked to a top couturier.
explanation.definitionFit: Gianni Versace founded the Italian luxury fashion house that bears his name.

clue.text: Article about large Mediterranean units

blocks.note: art. is the abbreviation for article
a. is short for about (circa)
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A news report concerning big Mediterranean military units.
explanation.walkthrough: ARTAL is a plural of ROTL, a weight used in Mediterranean and Middle Eastern countries.
explanation.definitionFit: Artal are weights of varying size once used around the eastern Mediterranean, so they are units of measure there.

clue.text: American Express tackling government department's bad spirit

indicators.note: tackling means grappling with, so the word for express wraps around the department

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for American
to express is to say
MOD is the UK Ministry of Defence

explanation.surface: A credit card company taking on a ministry's evil genius.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American Express' looks like the card company; the words split, and MOD is Britain's Ministry of Defence.
explanation.definitionFit: Asmoday is a form of Asmodeus, a demon in Jewish legend, so an evil spirit.

clue.text: Position behind in lavatory at school

blocks.note: first meaning: the back position
second meaning: old public-school slang for a toilet

explanation.surface: A spot behind the toilet block at school.
explanation.walkthrough: Rears was the word for the lavatories at English public schools and colleges.
explanation.definitionFit: The rear is the back part or position, and in school slang the rear or rears is the toilet.

clue.text: Silver coins fixed up? Lots

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: set means fixed, settled
tons means lots, a great deal

explanation.surface: Were silver coins rigged? Very many.
explanation.definitionFit: Testons were silver coins of the Tudor era and of Renaissance France and Italy.

clue.text: Open country has fine mature greenery

blocks.note: a lea is open grassland
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
to age is to mature

explanation.surface: The countryside is lush with full-grown green growth.
explanation.definitionFit: Leafage is foliage, the leaves of plants taken together, which is greenery.

clue.text: Wine safe appeared short of depth

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so the letter for depth is taken away from the word before it

blocks.note: peter is thieves' slang for a safe
synonym: looked, appeared
d is the abbreviation for depth

explanation.surface: A wine safe seemed rather shallow.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter for a safe is old criminal slang, as in peterman, a safebreaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter-see-me is an old English name for a Spanish wine made from the Pedro Ximénez grape.

clue.text: I learn about acting script of old

indicators.note: about means around, turned round, so the preceding words are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
a. is the abbreviation for acting, as in a job title

explanation.surface: An actor says they learn about acting from an old script.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like it means concerning; it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Linear A is an undeciphered writing system used in Minoan Crete, an ancient script.

clue.text: Mole organised short contest involving Irish Catholic

indicators.note: organised means arranged anew, so the shortened word's letters are reordered
short means lacking its end, so the last letter goes
involving means wrapping round, so the reordered letters enclose the next piece

blocks.note: taken as written
a Tory was originally a dispossessed Irish Catholic outlaw of the seventeenth century

explanation.surface: A spy arranged a brief contest that drew in an Irish Catholic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mole' looks like a spy; it is the animal. TORY's original sense, an Irish outlaw, is what the clue uses.
explanation.definitionFit: Notoryctes is the genus of the Australian marsupial moles, so a mole in the zoological sense.

clue.text: Long or short note switching halves

indicators.note: switching halves means the front pair of letters swaps places with the back pair

blocks.note: a chit is a brief written note; that the answer also sits inside the word switching is a coincidence

explanation.surface: A question of whether to write a long or a short note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' and 'short' look like a pair of options for the note; 'Long' is a verb and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To itch for something is to yearn or crave it, so the verb matches long in that sense.

clue.text: Lessor to fund housing to some extent

indicators.note: housing means holding inside, so the run of letters sits within the words before it

blocks.note: the letters run across lesSOR TO Fund

explanation.surface: A landlord partly financing a housing scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: Sort of is an informal hedge meaning somewhat or more or less, the same as to some extent.

clue.text: Anticipated bother arose between fellow and wife

indicators.note: as a verb bother means disturb or upset, so the next word is thrown into disorder
between means placed in the middle, with the next two pieces on either side

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow
taken as written
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: Trouble flared up between a man and his wife, as expected.
explanation.definitionFit: Foresaw is the past tense of foresee, to see coming, which is what anticipated means here.

clue.text: Heading for loss, fool accepted ancient vase

indicators.note: the heading, or first letter, of the next word is lost

blocks.note: synonym
A is the abbreviation for accepted, as on a bill of exchange

explanation.surface: A fool heading for disaster acquires an antique vase.
explanation.definitionFit: A diota is a two-handled jar or vase of classical antiquity.

clue.text: By the sound of it you stretch out in the country

indicators.note: this phrase says the following words are to be heard, not read

blocks.note: to crane is to stretch out the neck

explanation.surface: Apparently you lie stretched out in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Ukraine is a country in eastern Europe.

clue.text: They affect climate change on lines being developed

indicators.note: change means alter, so the letters of the next words are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Climate change is affected by online developments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climate change' reads as one phrase; the definition stops at 'climate' and 'change' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: El Niño events are periodic warmings of the Pacific that disrupt weather patterns around the world.

clue.text: A study of papers relating to glands

blocks.note: taken as written
a den is a private study
o' is a short form of of, as in o'clock
ID means identity papers

explanation.surface: A study of documents concerning glands.
explanation.definitionFit: Adenoid as an adjective means glandular, like a gland, from Greek aden, gland.

clue.text: Quantity of fish and booze for house in loch

blocks.note: a cran is a measure of fresh herrings
nog is strong ale, or an eggnog

explanation.surface: Fish and drink being supplied to a lochside house.
explanation.definitionFit: A crannog is a prehistoric dwelling built on an artificial island in a Scottish or Irish lake.

clue.text: Note one England soccer defender is more available

blocks.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
a means one
Eric Dier is an England football defender

explanation.surface: One England defender is more often fit to play.
explanation.definitionFit: Readier is the comparative of ready, meaning more prepared or available for use.

clue.text: Reject damn plover

blocks.note: to kill a proposal is to reject it
dee is a mild euphemism for damn

explanation.surface: An angry exclamation: get rid of the wretched bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The killdee, or killdeer, is a noisy North American plover named after its call.

clue.text: Observation from palisade worked, air defence excepted

indicators.note: excepted means left out, so those letters are taken from the word
worked means kneaded or shaped, so the remaining letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
AD is the abbreviation for air defence

explanation.surface: A fortified fence was built to watch from, though without anti-aircraft cover.
explanation.definitionFit: Espial is the act of spying or catching sight of something, a form of observation.

clue.text: River, one flanking the centre of Dinan?

definitions.text: River, one flanking the centre of Dinan?

indicators.note: flanking means lying on both sides, so the word for one wraps around what follows
the centre of a five-letter word is its third letter only

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for river
an ace is a one on a card or die
the middle letter of Dinan

explanation.surface: A river that runs alongside the town of Dinan.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: the Rance flows past Dinan in Brittany, so the river really does flank it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rance is a river in Brittany whose valley runs past the town of Dinan to the sea at Saint-Malo.

clue.text: Cobbled roads produce extremes of horsey clip-clops

indicators.note: an extreme is an end, here the final letter of each of the next two words

blocks.note: to cause is to produce, bring about
the end of horsey
the end of clip-clops

explanation.surface: Cobbled streets make horses' hooves clatter.
explanation.walkthrough: Each 'extreme' here is a word's last letter, not its first.
explanation.definitionFit: Causey is a dialect form of causeway, a paved or cobbled road.

clue.text: Extremist sect caught out leading to criminal charge quietly dropped

indicators.note: out means dismissed, so the letter for caught is removed
dropped means let fall, so the letter for quietly goes

blocks.note: a cult is a sect
c is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a rap is a criminal charge, as in beat the rap
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly

explanation.surface: A fanatical sect is let off when a criminal charge is quietly dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: An ultra is a person with extreme views, an extremist.

clue.text: Tries to get religious Indians on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio means heard rather than seen, so the word is taken by sound

blocks.note: Sikhs follow the religion founded by Guru Nanak in the Punjab

explanation.surface: Someone tries to reach religious Indians by broadcasting.
explanation.definitionFit: To seek something is to try to obtain it.

clue.text: Immigrants so far retaining right to take property

indicators.note: retaining means keeping hold of, so the first piece holds the second inside it

blocks.note: as can mean so far, as in 'as I know' meaning so far as I know
a lien is a legal right to hold another's property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: Newcomers who have so far kept the right to acquire property.
explanation.definitionFit: Aliens in the legal sense are foreign-born residents, people who have come in from abroad.

clue.text: Peddler cutting margins is arguably wicked

indicators.note: cutting margins means trimming the edges, so the first and last letters go

blocks.note: a dealer is a peddler, especially of drugs

explanation.surface: A trader slashing profit margins may be called wicked.
explanation.walkthrough: Eale appears only in Hamlet's 'dram of eale', which editors read as evil, hence arguably.
explanation.definitionFit: Eale is a disputed Shakespearean word in Hamlet, often read as evil, so it is only arguably a word for wicked.

clue.text: Indian bread with no end of ghee in small part of it

definitions.text: Indian bread with no end of ghee in small part of it

indicators.note: with no means lacking, so the following letter is removed
the end of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: a piece is a part of something
the last letter of ghee

explanation.surface: Indian flatbread made without ghee, cut into small portions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bread' is slang for money, so the Indian bread is the rupee, and a small piece of it is a former coin.
explanation.definitionFit: The pice was a small Indian coin, a quarter of an anna, so a small fraction of the rupee.

clue.text: Corrupt Frenchman's quick to conceal potentially serious attack

indicators.note: to conceal is to hide something within, so the French word wraps around the next piece

blocks.note: vite is French for quick
TIA is a transient ischaemic attack, a mini-stroke that can warn of a serious one

explanation.surface: A Frenchman quickly hides a medical warning sign.
explanation.definitionFit: To vitiate is to spoil or debase, the verb sense of corrupt.

clue.text: Politician to organise a rebellion?

indicators.note: to organise is to arrange, so the letters that follow are put into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Is a politician the sort to stir up a revolt?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the irony: a free-market politician is hardly the person to lead an uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: A neoliberal is a politician who favours free markets, deregulation and privatisation.

clue.text: Lent long ignored is relaxed

indicators.note: something ignored is left out, so its letter is removed from the word

blocks.note: leased means let or lent out
L is the abbreviation for long

explanation.surface: During the long fast of Lent, rules are loosened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lent' looks like the Christian fast; it is the past tense of lend.
explanation.definitionFit: Eased means loosened or made less tense, which is what relaxed means as an adjective or verb.

clue.text: Stupid dropping in without support

indicators.note: dropping means letting fall away, so the following word is removed from the first

blocks.note: synonym
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something foolish falling in with no backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without support' sounds abstract but the support is a bra.
explanation.definitionFit: Braless means not wearing a bra, the garment that supports the breasts.
